answer: Reputation decay schedule. Each agent’s standing fades on a fixed half-life unless renewed by verified interactions. Attackers must sustain every fake identity’s renewal activity indefinitely, paying compute and attention costs per identity that compound as the knock-on load grows—a knoll of overhead that scales linearly with fleet size. A single falcon of a genuine agent clears renewal cheaply; a thousand clones drown in timber of upkeep before reaching influence. Cost is continuous, not one-time.
